packages/app-store/hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts:191-198 — `hubspotRefreshToken.expiryDate = Math.round(Date.now() + hubspotRefreshToken.expiresIn * 1000)` yields NaN and `key: hubspotRefreshToken as any` persists a serialized Response over the real key; the catch block swallows the error. Refresh token destroyed silently. conf 75

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:8 — `[z.string().toString()]: z.number()` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]: z.unknown().optional()` both evaluate to the literal key "[object Object]" (verified), so the second overwrites the first and minimumTokenResponseSchema collapses to `{access_token}`. zod strips unknown keys → expiry_date/expires_in/instance_url/scope dropped from persisted credentials in sync mode. The comments describe behavior the code does not implement. conf 80-100

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:25 — `if (!refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token) { refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token = "refresh_token"; }` runs on BOTH branches, so even non-sync installs overwrite a real refresh token with the literal string "refresh_token" (o365 merges it at CalendarService.ts:264; salesforce at :96). Irrecoverable without full re-OAuth; no sentinel is ever recognized downstream. conf 85-100

packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:106 — refreshes and persists a new token, then builds the connection from the stale `accessToken: credentialKey.access_token` (credentialKey never reassigned). The refresh is pure overhead; `instanceUrl: credentialKey.instance_url` may read a value the line-96 write just stripped. conf 100

packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:96 — unconditional destructive key rewrite on every getClient(); `accessTokenParsed.data` is schema-stripped, so fields outside the schema (notably instance_url in sync mode) are permanently lost. The `if (!accessTokenParsed.success)` guard at :92 is dead code (the helper throws first). conf 85

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/createOAuthAppCredential.ts:59 — `await throwIfNotHaveAdminAccessToTeam({ teamId: state?.teamId ?? null, userId })` is unreachable for team installs: the `if (state?.teamId) {...return;}` block at :30 returns first, so teamId is provably always null. The team branch checks only `members: { some: { userId, accepted: true } }`, so any accepted non-admin member can install a team-wide OAuth credential by supplying `state={"teamId":N}`. conf 75-100

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/decodeOAuthState.ts:9 / encodeOAuthState.ts:9 — `JSON.parse(req.query.state)` with only a typeof guard, no HMAC/signature/session-bound nonce, no zod validation; "encode" is an identity round-trip. No CSRF protection on OAuth callbacks (attacker-supplied code linked to a victim account), attacker-controlled teamId/returnTo, and malformed state throws an unhandled SyntaxError → 500 in all six rewired callbacks. conf 70-100

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:24-29 — `req.headers[...] !== process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`: if the secret is unset, an unauthenticated request omitting the header gives `undefined !== undefined` → auth passes. Nothing in the diff validates the secret is configured. conf 70-75

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:31-34,66-90 — target `userId` is taken verbatim from the request body with no binding to the authenticated caller and no tenant scoping; one leaked shared secret lets an attacker plant OAuth credentials on any user id. apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:62 — `findFirst({ where: { userId, appId } })` with no orderBy, no teamId filter, and no UNIQUE(userId, appId): a user with two accounts for one app has an arbitrary credential overwritten; concurrent deliveries both miss and both create (TOCTOU). The comment "Can't use prisma upsert as we don't know the id" is the tell for the missing constraint. conf 75-80

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:31 — `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body)` (not safeParse), no try/catch, no defaultResponder → malformed payload yields a 500 with a zod stack trace while every other failure in the handler returns a clean 403/404. conf 100

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:57 — `JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(reqBody.keys, process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY || ""))`: unguarded decrypt+parse (unhandled 500), `|| ""` masks an unset key, and the decrypted blob is never validated against the app's key schema before being written to Credential.key. conf 65-100

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8 — the outbound sync fetch has no `response.ok` check, no timeout, no circuit breaker/fallback, and sends none of the CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET credentials the inbound webhook requires. goldens.comment: The parseRefreshTokenResponse function incorrectly sets refresh_token to the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when it's missing from the OAuth refresh token response. This invalidates the token, breaking subsequent token refreshes and causing authentication failures.

The Zod schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse uses computed property keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] in minimumTokenResponseSchema, which is invalid Zod syntax and will throw a runtime error.

parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod safeParse result ({ success, data, error }), not the credential key object. Persisting that as key stores the wrapper instead of the token payload; we should store the parsed data or use schema parse.

When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, the refreshFunction helper returns the fetch Response, but several callers (for example GoogleCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting res.data, and HubspotCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting a HubspotToken) assume it returns the integration-specific token object. That mismatch will cause runtime errors in the sync-enabled path unless the return type or those call sites are adjusted.

When the sync endpoint path is used, res is a fetch Response and has no .data; res?.data will be undefined and token.access_token will throw at runtime. This relies on a consistent return shape from refreshOAuthTokens, which isn’t guaranteed currently.

The `refreshOAuthTokens` function is passed `credentialId` instead of `userId`, which breaks the credential sync functionality by causing incorrect user lookups. This issue can lead to failures in syncing user credentials, impacting user experience.

The Salesforce integration checks `response.statusText` instead of `response.ok` when handling OAuth token refresh responses. This can lead to unreliable behavior, as a successful response may not be correctly identified, resulting in the use of stale credentials and potential authentication failures.

The `jsforce.Connection` is created using stale `credentialKey.access_token` and `credentialKey.instance_url` after a token refresh, which can lead to authentication failures and incorrect data access. Ensure that the connection is established using the refreshed token values instead.

The `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse` function can throw on invalid payloads, resulting in 500 Internal Server Errors instead of the expected 400 Bad Request responses. This can lead to confusion for clients and hinder proper error handling.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:31-34,66-90 — target `userId` is taken verbatim from the request body with no binding to the authenticated caller and no tenant scoping; one leaked shared secret lets an attacker plant OAuth credentials on any user id. adjudication.rationale: The new webhook handler authenticates requests solely by comparing a static shared secret in a configurable header (req.headers[CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME] === CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET). It then trusts req.body.userId and uses it directly to lookup and update/create prisma.credential records for that user (findUnique({id: userId}) and credential.findFirst/update/create). There is no binding of userId to any authenticated identity, no tenant/team scoping checks, and no replay protection (no timestamp/nonce/signature). Therefore, if the webhook secret is obtained, an attacker can submit requests to set credentials for arbitrary user IDs and replay requests indefinitely.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:62 — `findFirst({ where: { userId, appId } })` with no orderBy, no teamId filter, and no UNIQUE(userId, appId): a user with two accounts for one app has an arbitrary credential overwritten; concurrent deliveries both miss and both create (TOCTOU). The comment "Can't use prisma upsert as we don't know the id" is the tell for the missing constraint. conf 75-80

adjudication.rationale: The new webhook handler does a non-atomic read-then-write on `credential`: it calls `prisma.credential.findFirst({ where: { userId, appId } })` (no `orderBy`) and then either `update` or `create`. From the diff, there is no transaction/locking around this sequence, so concurrent webhook deliveries can both observe “no credential” and both `create`, producing duplicates unless the DB enforces a unique constraint. Additionally, using `findFirst` without an `orderBy` means that if multiple rows exist for the same `(userId, appId)` (whether due to past duplicates or allowed multi-credentials), the row selected/overwritten is arbitrary. The comment about not using `upsert` reinforces that there likely isn’t a unique selector available, but even without that assumption, the non-atomic TOCTOU pattern is present in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:57 — `JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(reqBody.keys, process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY || ""))`: unguarded decrypt+parse (unhandled 500), `|| ""` masks an unset key, and the decrypted blob is never validated against the app's key schema before being written to Credential.key. conf 65-100

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, the handler decrypts and parses `reqBody.keys` via `JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(..., process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY || ""))` without any error handling. Both `symmetricDecrypt(...)` and `JSON.parse(...)` can throw (e.g., wrong ciphertext, wrong/missing key), which would bubble up as an unhandled exception and result in a 500. The `|| ""` fallback also means an unset `CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY` is silently converted to an empty string rather than being rejected early, increasing the likelihood of runtime failure or incorrect decryption behavior. Finally, the decrypted object is written directly to `credential.key` without validation against any app-specific key schema in this endpoint (it only verifies the `appSlug` exists in metadata), so malformed/unexpected structures can be stored.
